questions.stem: A hydraulic press has a 2-square-inch input piston and a 50-square-inch output piston. If 100 pounds of force is applied to the input and losses are ignored, what output force is produced?

250 pounds

4 pounds

questions.stem: During a tank pressure calculation, solve the following problem and select the best answer: A gauge tap is 36 ft below the free surface of a water tank. Ignoring losses, what hydrostatic pressure is expected at the tap?
options: 15.6 psi
83.1 psi
2.4 psi
36.0 psi
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: For water, pressure is approximately P = 0.433*h. Thus 0.433*36 ft = 15.588 psi, or 15.6 psi.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This divides head by 0.433, which calculates equivalent head from pressure instead.
This reverses the conversion and understates the pressure.
This treats feet of head as numerically equal to psi.

options: 451 ft
120 ft
225 ft
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Rearrange P = 0.433*h to h = P/0.433. Then 52/0.433 = 120.1 ft, approximately 120 ft.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This divides by the square of 0.433 without justification.
This uses an incorrect conversion of about 0.231 psi per foot.
This multiplies pressure by 0.433 instead of dividing.

This uses only sqrt(2*h) and omits gravitational acceleration.

questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Convert diameter to 0.333 ft. Area = pi*d^2/4 = 0.0873 ft^2, so Q = A*v = 0.0873*9.0 = 0.785 ft^3/s.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This applies pi directly to the velocity without calculating area.
This multiplies velocity by diameter rather than the pipe cross-sectional area.
This uses radius as though it were diameter in the circular-area calculation.

options: 8.9 ft
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Velocity head is hv = v^2/(2*g) = 24^2/(2*32.2) = 8.94 ft, or 8.9 ft.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This reports the denominator 2g as the answer.

options: 21 ft
55 ft
646 ft
38 ft
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The pump must lift from 38 ft below grade to 17 ft above grade, so static head is 38 + 17 = 55 ft.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This subtracts the elevations even though the suction and discharge are on opposite sides of grade.
This multiplies the two elevations rather than finding their vertical difference.
This includes only the suction lift and omits the discharge elevation.

questions.stem: At a buoyancy and displacement problem, a supervisor proposes: "A check valve installed in place of pressure relief". The underlying case is: A positive-displacement pump can continue building pressure against a closed discharge valve. Which protection is essential?
